To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified specific and quantitative cilia beating anomalies, according, to the cilia ultrastructure, in patients with primary ciliary dyskenesia.

we performed deep phenotyping of ciliary beating in primary ciliary dysfunction (PCD), including 75 patients with different ciliary ultrastructural defects, and identified specific quantitative ciliary beating defects, which are associated with specific cilia ultrastructures and genotyping.

quantitative high-speed video-micrsocopy of ciliary beating in patients with primary ciliary dyskenisia (PCD) reveals specific and quantitative anomalies associated with the different ultrastructural phenotypes and genotypes, and that this approach represents a promising strategy to guide the molecular analysis of PCD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the ciliary beat pattern in primary ciliary dysfunction (PCD).

the study of the molecular basis of primary ciliary dysgenesis (PCD), a rare genetic disease affecting the ciliary structure and/or motility and leading to respiratory tract infections and infertility in affected individuals.
a rare genetic disorder, PCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ultrastructural phenotype is the key to understand the pathophysiology of PCD and to predict the clinical outcome.
the ultrastructural phenotypes are the best predictors of the ciliary beating anomalies and, consequently, of the most probable PCD gene(s) involved in the disease.
ciliary beating parameters are not only a matter of ciliary ultrastructure and genotype, but also a matter of the ciliated cell type, the cell culture technique, and the HSV technique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ciliary beating parameters are not only quantitative but are specific for each ultrastructural defect.
the ciliary beating parameters can help to identify the ciliary defect, but not the gene involved.
the ciliary beating phenotype is highly dependent on the underlying ciliary ultrastructural defects, and this is true even for the same ultrastructural defect, when it is caused by different genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cilia beat frequency is a very good marker of PCD and that the cilia beating pattern is also very informative.
ciliary beating parameters can be used to predict ciliary ultrastructure and to guide molecular analysis in PCD patients.
